# Trustworthy and Transferable Water Demand Forecasting

[REDACTED]

Replication package for the article *Trustworthy and Transferable Water
Demand Forecasting: A Cross-Country Real-World Study* (Maußner & Teppan,
Expert Systems with Applications). It contains the complete source code,
the input data, and the raw result files of every experiment reported in
the paper.

Everything in `results_unified/` and `results_cards/` was produced by the
code in this repository on the single laptop documented in Section 9 of
the article. The figures and tables of the manuscript are generated from
those result files, not from a separate analysis.

## What is benchmarked

Eighteen forecasting approaches in six groups, applied to 261 real
demand series from three countries under one leakage-free protocol:

| Group | Approaches |
| --- | --- |
| Naive | NAIVE1, SNAIVE7 |
| Tabular ML | LR, KNN, SVR-LIN, SVR-RAD, RF, XGB |
| Classical | SARIMA, SARIMAX |
| Deep sequence | LSTM, XLSTM, TFT, CNN-GRU |
| Pretrained, zero-shot | CHRONOS, TIMESFM, TIREX2, TIREX2-X |

`TIREX2` and `TIREX2-X` are the univariate and the covariate arm of one
TiRex-2 checkpoint. Model names are written in capitals throughout the
code and the result files; the article uses the vendors' spelling in
running text.

## Layout

```
code/
  code_unified/   Austrian and Italian benchmark, transfer experiments,
                  significance tests, figures and tables (E1-E7, E10)
  code_cards/     Californian external validation at scale (E8, E9)
data/
  Austria/        city and district inflow, SPARTACUS climate grid
  Italy/          pre-processed daily features of the ten BWDF districts
  CaRDS/          Californian supplier cross-section
results_unified/  raw results, per-series predictions, figures, tables
results_cards/    the same for the external validation
paper/            the accepted manuscript as PDF
```

## Environments

Three Python environments are required, because the pretrained models
impose mutually incompatible version constraints. This is a property of
the upstream packages, not of this code.

| Environment | Python | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | 3.12.10 | classical models, deep models, all analyses and figures |
| B | 3.14.6 | Chronos-Bolt and TimesFM inference |
| C | 3.12 | TiRex-2 inference (requires an interpreter below 3.14) |

```bash
pip install -r requirements-tensorflow.txt   # A
pip install -r requirements-torch.txt        # B
pip install -r requirements-tirex.txt        # C
```

## Reproducing the results

Run from inside the respective code directory. Every runner is
incremental: results are appended, `--skip-existing` resumes, and
`--max-seconds` splits a long experiment into chunks.

Environment A:

```bash
cd code/code_unified
python run_experiments.py            # E1, the locally trained approaches
python run_deep_repeats.py           # five repetitions per sequence model
python run_cnngru.py                 # adds the CNN-GRU to E1 and E2
python run_ablation_covariates.py    # E2, four nested information sets
python run_transfer.py               # E3, IT -> AT
python run_transfer_reverse.py       # E4, AT -> IT
python run_transfer_italy.py         # E5 to E7 within Italy
python run_stats.py                  # Diebold-Mariano, Friedman-Nemenyi
python make_all_figures.py           # every figure and table of the paper
python make_appendix.py              # appendix tables
```

Environment B, then C:

```bash
python run_foundation.py             # Chronos-Bolt, zero-shot
python run_foundation2.py            # TimesFM 2.5, zero-shot
python run_foundation3.py            # TiRex-2, univariate and covariate arms
```

External validation (environment A, plus B and C for the pretrained
arms):

```bash
cd code/code_cards
python run_cards_experiments.py      # local benchmark on 249 suppliers
python run_cards_transfer.py         # E8, source-diversity curve
python run_cards_selection.py        # E9, informed selection at scale
python run_foundation_cards.py       # pretrained models on CaRDS
python run_foundation_cards2.py
python make_cards_figures.py
```

`make_figures.py` has no entry point of its own on purpose: several
generators are defined late in the file, so running it directly would
produce a partial set. Always use `make_all_figures.py`.

## Notes on reproducibility

Seeds are fixed at 42. The tabular models, the ARIMA family and the
zero-shot models reproduce bit-identically. The four sequence models do
not: seeding fixes weight initialisation and shuffling, but not the
reduction order of multi-threaded CPU kernels, and early stopping turns
small numerical differences into different stopping epochs. Every
sequence-model entry in the paper is therefore the median of five runs,
produced by `run_deep_repeats.py`, which stores all individual runs in
`results_unified/results_deep_repeats.csv`.

TiRex-2 was executed in eager mode; its compiled fast path needs a C++
toolchain the reference machine does not provide, so its reported
runtimes are upper bounds.

## Data and licences

Code is released under the MIT licence (`LICENSE`). Data are released
under CC BY 4.0 (`LICENSE-DATA`).

The Austrian series are published with the explicit permission of
Stadtwerke Klagenfurt. They are aggregated at city and district level
and contain no household-level information; the underlying per-household
exports are deliberately not part of this package. The Italian districts
are the pre-processed daily features derived from the Battle of the
Water Demand Forecasting dataset, the Californian cross-section from the
public CaRDS dataset. Both are redistributed under the terms of their
original licences, cited in the article.

## Citation

See `CITATION.cff`. Please cite the article and, if you use the package
itself, the archived release at
[10.5281/zenodo.21997262](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21997262).
